newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FULL TEXT-Industrial Relations Commission decision.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Industrial Relations Commission decision.

text.p: The following is the full text of the safety net wage review announced by the full bench of the Australian Industrial Relations Commission on Tuesday:

"Our decision, among other matters, relates to applications made by a number of unions to give effect to the first stage of a three stage claim, which the Australian Council of Trade Unions (ACTU) has described as a Living Wage Claim.

The first stage of the ACTU's Living Wage Claim, in summary, seeks the establishment of a minimum award rate of pay of $10 per hour for work in ordinary hours (or, $380 per 38 hour week) with increases in other award rates to maintain relativities and a "safety net adjustment" of $20 per week.

We do not grant the ACTU's claim. We are, however, of the view that there should be an adjustment to the arbitrated safety net. There is, however, a differing opinion among us as to the quantum of this adjustment having regard to the most appropriate balance between the economic and social factors we have taken into account.
With respect to the claim the majority decision is:
(1) to award an arbitrated safety net adjustment of $10 per week;

(2) to determine a minimum wage (to be called the 'Federal minimum wage') for full-time adult employees of $359.40 per week and, for junior, part-time and casual employees, of a proportionate amount. (The Federal minimum wage is to be inclusive of the arbitrated safety net adjustment determined by this decision and all previous safety net and national wage adjustments.)
(3) to provide that increases under both (1) and (2) are fully absorbable against all above award payments;
(4) to provide for the variation of both minimum rates and paid rates awards;

(5) to provide that any outstanding $8 per week arbitrated safety net adjustments granted by previous decisions be available from the same date as the $10 per week arbitrated safety net adjustment available pursuant to this decision;

(6) to provide for the commencement of award variations to give effect to this decision to occur no earlier than the date on which the award is varied, except that provision will be made for the phasing-in of increases where circumstances justify it;

(7) to permit the expression of award rates, by consent of all parties, and where the minimum rates adjustment has been completed, as hourly rates as well as weekly rates. In the absence of consent, a claim that award rates be so expressed may be determined by arbitration; and

(8) to provide that allowances which relate to work or conditions which have not changed and service increments be adjusted as a result of the $10 per week arbitrated safety net increase. (The method of adjustment is to be consistent with the Furnishing and Glass Industries Allowances decision Print M9675.) The majority decision has, among other things:
(1) referred to the need to balance the legislative requirements with respect to awards and to agreements;
(6) examined the living standards and the needs of the low paid in determining the nature and amount of the award increases, within the constraints imposed by economic factors.

The majority decision is made in the context of the present wages system in which the making of agreements between employees and employers at the workplace or enterprise is the prime method of regulating wages. This system has had, and at present has, the general support of the industrial parties and the Federal and State Governments.

The majority is satisfied that its decision fully meets the test of fairness in the current economic circumstances. It would have liked to award a larger increase if it could responsibly have done so. However, it was constrained in this regard by the present level of unemployment in Australia. The issue of employment is a complex one and the majority has addressed it at some length in its decision.
(2) expressed the view that the key factor in "a safety net of fair minimum wages and conditions of employment" s.88B(2) is fairness;
(3) expressed the view that the award system, as it exists from time to time, will remain the safety net of fair minimum wages (and condeitions of employment);
(4) considered the cost of the ACTU wage claim and counter-proposals to it;
(5) considered the effect of wage increases on employment and the relation between wages, pricws and productivity;

We publish our majority decision.
Vice President Ross does not agree with the quantum of the arbitrated safety net increase awarded by the majority nor with the conditions attached to that increase.
In the circumstances of this case, His Honour would have awarded a safety net adjustment of:
- A$15 per week for persons employed at or below classification level C7 (i.e. A$503.80) in the metal Industry Award 1984 - Part I, or its equivalent; and

For the future, much depends upon the effect on bargaining outcomes of a transition from an inflationary to a non-inflationary environment. If past agreement outcomes have been fuelled by "going-rate" notions which belong to an inflationary world, there is a prospect that the progressive recognition of the new, non-inflationary environment will lower the level of settlements so as to leave "space" for a more generous treatement of workers fully or substantially dependent on award wages. Unless this occurs, the Commission may be faced with either accepting a growing disparity between levels in the two sectors or seeking to reduce the disparity in a manner which
- 2.5 percent for persons employed above classificaton level C7.

This safety net adjustment would have been provided in two instalments six months apart, subject to a number of tests including the provision of union commitments to full absorption and the establishment of a program of discussions to deal with the award review process. In His Honour's view the facilitation of the award review process should be given specific encouragement by the provision of a linkage with arbitrated safety net adjustments.
His Honour's decision is published with the majority decision.
BY THE COMMISSION."
